description:
FILED s471a (Opus, 2026-09-06), by a #1271 probe.  PRE-EXISTING.

    open(my $fh, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die;
    ref($fh)

    perl 5.40.3 : GLOB
    PCL         : "" (empty)

`"$fh"` already stringifies GLOB-ishly and `defined`/truthiness are right, so
only `ref` (and `reftype`, and anything that dispatches on them) diverges.

THE CAUSE is one line: `%p-install-fh`'s last box arm is `(box-set fh stream)`,
i.e. the box holds the CL STREAM object directly.  A glob ref would be a box
with `is-ref` set holding a `p-typeglob`, which is what
`%p-autoviv-failed-handle` (#1271, s471a) now installs on the FAILURE path --
so PCL currently gives a failed open a more perl-shaped handle than a
successful one.

DO NOT fix this by making the success path install a glob without measuring:
`%p-resolve-fh` reaches a stream in a box directly (`(streamp v) v`) and a glob
by NAME through `*p-filehandles*`, so moving every successful lexical open onto
the glob path routes every read and write through a hash lookup keyed by a
generated name, and the typeglob fallback in %p-resolve-fh compares symbol
NAMES across packages.  That is a performance AND a collision question, on the
hottest IO path there is.  Measure both before designing.

Code that greps `ref($fh) eq 'GLOB'` to decide whether it holds a handle is the
population this blocks; IO::Handle-style shims are the obvious users.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
FIXED as shape (b), and the task's warning was right to demand a measurement.
Two shapes were on the table and the numbers decided (20 M calls, sbcl 2.6.0,
scratch/s473f/shape-a-cost.lisp):

  shape (b), SHIPPED -- the box keeps the raw stream and ref/reftype read it:
      (streamp v)                      3.7 ns   (unchanged: the arm
                                                 %p-resolve-fh already takes)
  shape (a), REJECTED -- a p-typeglob on the success path, so every read and
  print reaches the stream by NAME:
      (find-symbol NAME) + gethash    32.1 ns   = +28 ns PER I/O OP

A third variant -- putting the openness test in `p-get-stream` -- was written
and backed out: `open-stream-p` is 7.9 ns against `streamp`'s 3.7, and
tools/bench-exec.pl's NEW fhprint/fhread rows measured it at -6.4 % / -4.0 %
against an otherwise-identical runtime.  As shipped those rows read +1.2 % /
+0.8 % (controls +0.9 / +0.8 / -2.8).

THE RULE: a box holding a stream or socket IS PCL's spelling of the glob ref
perl leaves in the scalar, so ref() and reftype() answer GLOB and `\$fh`
answers REF.  The string half already agreed (GLOB(0x...)) -- that
disagreement between the word and the string is how the bug was visible.  ONE
predicate %p-handle-payload-p, read by p-ref, %p-ref-string and (so that
`ref($a[0])` on an element handle agrees) the two element unboxers.

RESIDUE, filed: #1424 -- `my $g = *$fh; ref(\$g)` is REF where perl says GLOB.
PCL has no is-ref flag on a handle payload, so it cannot tell a glob VALUE from
a glob REF; keeping the box test right for the COMMON shapes (`my $b = $fh`,
`ref($a[0])`) costs this exotic one.  Commit 42676dff.
subject: A SUCCESSFUL `open(my $fh, ...)` leaves ref($fh) = "" where perl says GLOB: the success path box-sets the raw CL stream, so the box is not a glob ref
